subject: Hosted API commit/ramp proposal — request for step-up schedule and overage terms
messages:
From: Elise Carter <elise@novaflow.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API pricing for Q1 launch — commit/ramp questions

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the model latency and cost profile look promising for our product launch in Q1. We need to nail down pricing and a commit schedule so our finance and procurement teams can budget. A few specific asks from procurement:

- Example monthly commit/ramp schedules for a 3–6 month launch timeline (step-up commits).
- How per-token volume discounts are applied (thresholds, lookback period).
- Overage rates if we exceed committed volume in a month.
- Billing cadence and true-up mechanics.
- Any launch/intro credits or one-time promos for early customers.

We have a rough forecast attached (usage_forecast.xlsx) with expected traffic spikes around launch day and during staging. Can you send a concrete proposal and an example invoice math? Procurement would like to review by the end of next week.

Best,
Elise
VP Product
Novaflow

[Attachment: usage_forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet, 58 KB)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Elise Carter <elise@novaflow.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Nov 2025 10:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing for Q1 launch — commit/ramp questions

Hi Elise — really appreciate the forecast, that makes this much easier. I ran numbers with our solutions team and attached a short proposed commit schedule (proposed_commit_schedule.pdf) and worked example of monthly True-up math. High level proposal below — happy to sync on a 30-minute call to walk through.

Proposed monthly step-up commit (example for launch ramp):
- Month 1 (staging/soft-launch): 500,000 tokens committed
- Month 2 (initial launch): 1,500,000 tokens committed
- Month 3 (scale): 3,000,000 tokens committed
- Month 4+ (steady growth): optional increase to 5,000,000 tokens (by mutual agreement)

Discounting (hosted per-token):
- Baseline list: $0.00090/token
- Commit tier discounts (applied to committed units):
  - 0–1M: 10% off list
  - 1M–3M: 20% off list
  - 3M+: 30% off list

Overage and on‑demand behavior:
- If usage in a billing month exceeds committed units, overage is billed at committed-discount price + 20% overage premium (i.e., 1.2x the committed effective price).
- If you opt to exceed capacity frequently, we can discuss a Dedicated reservation for peak days.

Billing cadence and true-up:
- Monthly invoicing against committed units. Consumption above commit is billed on the next invoice as overage.
- Quarterly true-up for aggregate volume discounts if we agreed to multi-month lookbacks (can be included in contract).

Intro options for launch ramps:
- One-time $10,000 launch credit applied to first invoice (to help cover staging costs) OR
- Temporary 5% additional discount for first two months on committed units (mutually exclusive with the $10k credit).

Next steps: please let me know which ramp profile lines up with your forecast and whether procurement prefers a capped overage or lower overage premium — I can run alternate math.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0193

[Attachment: proposed_commit_schedule.pdf (document, 120 KB)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 08:34:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Hosted API pricing for Q1 launch — commit/ramp questions (internal)

Rishi / Marissa — forwarding Novaflow's ask and my proposed tiers. Key points: they want a gentle step-up ramp with big spikes at launch day. Forecast attached.

Questions for approval before I reply:
- Do we want to accept a 20% overage premium, or can we offer 10–15% for launch customers?
- Can we approve the $10k launch credit if they choose that option (refund applied to first invoice)?
- If we give a temporary extra discount for months 1–2, what guardrails do we need (min commit, month-to-month opt-out)?

My recommendation: offer a compromise — 15% overage premium and the $10k credit (or 5% extra discount) but require a three-month minimum commit schedule to qualify. If they're pushing back, we can do the 5% ephemeral discount instead of the credit.

Rishi — can you sign off on approval to make pricing exceptions for early Q1 launch partners? Marissa — can you prepare a sample contract clause about the ramp and true-up?

Thanks,
Soojin

> On Tue, Nov 11, 2025 at 10:07 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> > [proposed_commit_schedule.pdf attached]

From: Elise Carter <elise@novaflow.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@novaflow.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Nov 2025 13:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing for Q1 launch — commit/ramp questions

Thanks, Soojin — the proposal is helpful. Procurement reviewed and sent back a counter that fits our cashflow and risk profile:

Counter-proposed step-up commits:
- Month 1: 500,000 tokens committed (staging)
- Month 2: 1,500,000 tokens committed
- Month 3: 3,000,000 tokens committed
- Month 4: 5,000,000 tokens committed (optional, confirmed 30 days prior)

Counter requests / asks:
- Reduce overage premium to 10% (instead of 20%).
- If we exceed committed volume by more than 50% in any month, can you agree to a capped overage surcharge instead of linear pricing?
- Provide a one-page SLA for Hosted API availability during the launch window (expected 99.5% for peak time).
- We will sign a 3-month minimum commitment with the step-up schedule above, but need the right to pause increases in Month 4 with 30-days notice.

Attached an executive summary for their CFO with their preferred schedule and projected cashflows (executive_summary.pdf). Procurement is pushing for lower upfront spend; they prefer the overage cap versus a large launch credit.

Can you respond with a final math summary and I’ll circulate to procurement and finance?

Best,
Elise

[Attachment: executive_summary.pdf (document, 85 KB)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Elise Carter <elise@novaflow.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Nov 2025 15:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing for Q1 launch — commit/ramp questions

Hi Elise — thanks for the clear counteroffer and the exec summary; appreciate procurement's framing. We discussed internally and can do the following compromise designed to protect both sides during a high-variance launch: 

Final compromise proposal:
- Commit schedule: accept the step-up commits you outlined (500k / 1.5M / 3M / optional 5M).
- Overages: cap the overage premium at 15% (i.e., overage billed at committed effective price +15%).
  - If monthly usage > 150% of committed units, overage above that threshold will be billed at on-demand list price (no additional premium).
- Launch protection: we will provide a one-time $10,000 launch credit applied to the first invoice OR, if you prefer, we can substitute a 5% additional committed-unit discount for Months 1–2. (Pick one.)
- SLA: we'll provide a short Hosted API SLA addendum for the 60-day launch window (99.5% availability target) — legal to produce.
- Contract: I'll attach our redlines to the MSA. If this looks good I can send a DocuSign for signature (link below).

Why this compromise: 15% overage keeps us aligned on cost recovery while capping worst-case for you; the >150% rule prevents repeated large bursts from being subsidized. The $10k credit helps cashflow without lowering our base economics permanently.

Next steps:
1) Confirm whether you want the $10k credit or the 5% temporary discount.
2) If approved, we’ll circulate an updated MSA with the ramp schedule and SLA addendum.
3) Sign via DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/nd/signer/embeddedSign?token=ec-abcdef123456

Attaching: MSA_redlines.pdf (highlights on commit & overage clauses).

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if procurement wants to talk through the invoice math live.

Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0193

[Attachment: MSA_redlines.pdf (document, 48 KB)]
